subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• National parks provide crucial protection for wildlife habitats and natural ecosystems.
• Before the National Park Service was established, parks were managed by individual superintendents.
• Charles Gould was the superintendent of Yellowstone National Park in Wyoming.
• He held this position from 1872 to 1884.
• John Muir was the founding president of the Sierra Club in California.
• He held this position from 1892 to 1914.
prompt: The student wants to emphasize the order in which the two conservationists began their leadership roles. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: From 1872 to 1884, the natural landscapes of Wyoming were better protected thanks to conservationists John Muir and Charles Gould.
choices.B: John Muir began his leadership role as a conservationist years after Charles Gould did.
choices.C: Before the National Park Service was established, conservationists like Charles Gould and John Muir were crucial to protecting natural ecosystems.
choices.D: Charles Gould's role as a park superintendent ended in 1884, whereas John Muir's role as Sierra Club president ended in 1914.

explanation:
Choice B is correct. It emphasizes order: Muir became Sierra Club president in 1892 years after Gould became Yellowstone superintendent in 1872.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect because it makes a generalization about the effects of Muir's and Gould's work; it doesn't emphasize the order in which the two conservationists began their leadership roles. In addition, the sentence misrepresents information from the notes; Muir was the president of the Sierra Club in California from 1892 to 1914, not involved with protecting Wyoming from 1872 to 1884.
